newsitem.title: USA: US productivity growth may be picking up -- Rivlin.
newsitem.headline: US productivity growth may be picking up -- Rivlin.

text.p: Federal Reserve Vice Chair Alice Rivlin said on Wednesday that she saw signs that productivity growth was picking up, but doubted that it would double from its recent pace.
"There are some indications it is moving up," she told the House Banking Committee. "But a doubling? I doubt it," she added.
Productivity has recently been growing at rate of about one percent or slightly more per year.
Rivlin also told the lawmakers that the consumer price index may overstate inflation by 0.5 percentage point.
But she added that it does not have any significance for monetary policy because the overstatement has generally been constant over time and has not changed recently.
